proof_summary: Define the candidate sequence by \(B_0=4,B_1=16,B_2=63\) and \(B_{n+3}=4B_{n+2}-B_n\), and study \(\Delta_n=B_n^2-B_{n-1}B_{n+1}\). Positivity and growth of \(B_n\), together with \(\Delta_{k+4}=4\Delta_{k+2}+\Delta_{k+1}\), give \(0<\Delta_n<B_{n-1}\); hence \(B_{n+1}B_{n-1}<B_n^2\le (B_{n+1}+1)B_{n-1}\), so the ceiling-minus-one rule produces \(B_{n+1}\), and induction identifies the original sequence with the linear-recurrence sequence.
